brief_extract:
THE EAW STORY
by MARY GEORGE, CBE, Companion IEE, Director EAW

IN this Golden Jubilee year of the EAW when we are so much in the news people often ask how our Association came to be started. Our story began in a Mayfair drawing room on November 12, 1924 at 4.30 p.m.

title: Sir
brief_context: Hosted the informal tea party where EAW story began.

title: Lady
brief_context: President of WES; hosted the initial meeting at her home.
brief_extract: Our story began in a Mayfair drawing room on November 12, 1924 at 4.30 p.m. The occasion was an informal tea party at the home of Sir Charles and Lady Parsons and the guests included a number of distinguished men and women prominent in electrical and other fields. The object of the party was to gain support for a scheme conceived by the Women's Engineering Society of which Lady Parsons was President — a scheme for encouraging the domestic use of electricity through the formation of a Women's Electrical Association.

title: Mrs
brief_context: Originator of the scheme and speaker at the initial meeting.

title: Miss
associated_organisation: Women's Engineering Society (WES); Electrical Association for Women (EAW)
brief_context: Secretary of WES and later full-time Director of EAW.
brief_extract:
L. Matthews, the originator of the scheme, and Miss Caroline Haslett the then Secretary of the Women's Engineering Society, the party carried with acclamation, before it broke up, the following resolution:
"That this meeting of representative persons, realising the need to interest women in regard to electrical development in this country, decides to form a Women's Electrical Association, and wishes to put on record its thanks to Mrs Matthews for the initial step in contributing her paper on this subject."

Revolutionary effect on the home
It is interesting to note that it was the members of the Women's Engineering Society — professional women engineers -- who foresaw the revolutionary effect on the home that the advances in electrical development would have and who realised that the woman in the home would need to be prepared for the changes that were in store for her. The members of the WES had also seen in the course of their own work how labour-saving techniques were contributing to the efficiency and productivity of workers in factories and they were aware of the scope there was for applying labour-saving methods in the home.

title: Dr
brief_context: Referred to the association in his Faraday Lecture in 1928.
brief_extract:
First branch
The first branch of the EAW was formed in Glasgow in November 1925. Birmingham, Manchester and Newcastle-upon-Tyne quickly followed suit and by 1928 the Association was so well established, together with its journal "The Electrical Age" founded in 1926, that it was referred to by Dr Ferranti in his Faraday Lecture that year in the following words:
"Most happily there has arisen a new great force in the Electrical Association for Women. It is very new, but it already has enrolled 2,000 members, and, having regard to the difficulties connected with a new enterprise, I think this shows that there must be a surprisingly large number of women in the country who are keenly interested in matters electrical.

by MARY GEORGE, CBE, Companion IEE, Director EAW

THE EAW branches have followed the Sir Christopher Wren tradition in com- memorating the Association's Golden Jubilee since they have provided 'monuments' all over the country which will act as a reminder of this eventful year and of the continuing activities of the EAW for all who 'look around'. brief_context: Mentioned in description of Privy Council ceremonial procedures.
brief_extract: There is a special ceremonial uniform for the men but not for the women! At meetings the Lord President of the Council is received by the Queen and goes over the items to be discussed while those members of the Council directly concerned with the Bills or other matters wait outside and are then received by Her Majesty in the order of their appointment to the Council. The ceremony of appointment is impressive, one takes the oath and then receives a copy of the New Testament inscribed by the President of the Council.

title: Miss
brief_context: Interviewing the new EAW President about her message to members.
brief_extract: One then kneels to kiss the hand of the Monarch and then joins one's colleagues standing in line. Miss George: Finally, do you think as our new President you could give a message to the members of the Association? Lady Hornsby-Smith: With the multiplicity of electrical equipment and the increasing use of electrical appliances together with the 'do it yourself' trend it is increasingly important that families, and I emphasise families, should be educated in the basic principles of electricity and its safe use.
